claim.pdf_says: where property-specifier is:  /  PROPERTY property-name-1 [ AS literal-4 ]   and   where user-defined-function-specifier is:  /  FUNCTION function-prototype-name-1 [ AS literal-5 ]  -- printed as general-format skeletons, with PROPERTY, AS, FUNCTION and the second AS UNDERLINED (required words); property-name-1, literal-4, function-prototype-name-1 and literal-5 are not underlined.
claim.markdown_says: PROPERTY property-name-1 [ AS literal-4 ]  /      FUNCTION function-prototype-name-1 [ AS literal-5 ]  (plain indented prose lines -- no code fence, no <u>...</u>, and no "Figure notes" paragraph naming the underlined words.)
claim.why_it_matters: The underline is the only marker that distinguishes a REQUIRED word from an optional/comment word that may be omitted. Because AS sits inside brackets, losing its underline turns "[ AS literal-4 ]" into a phrase whose AS could legally be dropped while literal-4 is written -- falsely permissive here, and in the general case the same loss reads as falsely restrictive. These are the last two of the six REPOSITORY specifier formats: the four printed on page 334 (class-, interface-, intrinsic-function- and program-specifier) are each code-fenced WITH a Figure notes paragraph listing the underlined words, and pages 341 and 343 in this same batch mark inline formats with <u>FILE-CONTROL</u> and <u>SELECT</u> [ <u>OPTIONAL</u> ]. So the convention exists and only these two figures lost it.

verdict.reasoning: CONFIRMED on both sides, and the claim is quoted accurately. (1) PDF side -- I rendered spec_p335.png at 300 dpi and cropped/upscaled the two format lines (E:/Temp/specrecon/v335/crop_formats.png). Reading the printed glyphs directly: 'PROPERTY property-name-1 [ AS literal-4 ]' shows a continuous rule under the seven letters P-R-O-P-E-R-T-Y and a separate short rule under the two letters A-S; 'FUNCTION function-prototype-name-1 [ AS literal-5 ]' shows a rule under F-U-N-C-T-I-O-N and a short rule under A-S. No rule appears beneath property-name-1, literal-4, function-prototype-name-1 or literal-5, and none beneath the brackets. Both lines are set indented, in the two-blank-line general-format style, not as running prose. (2) Markdown side -- specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 14513 and 14517 (page-335.md lines 8 and 12) are '    PROPERTY property-name-1 [ AS literal-4 ]' and '    FUNCTION function-prototype-name-1 [ AS literal-5 ]'. I read the surrounding 90 lines: there is no ``` fence, no <u>, and no '> **Figure notes' paragraph after either line. All four markers are genuinely absent, not reflowed onto an adjacent line. (3) Not merely formatting -- the underline carries normative meaning that the transcription drops. Spec Sec 5.2.3 (Optional words): 'Optional words are reserved words or context-sensitive words. They are shown in uppercase and not underlined in general formats. They may be written to add clarity...'; Sec 8.3.2.4.3 (Optional words): 'Within each format, uppercase words that are not underlined are called optional words and may be specified at the user's option with no effect on the semantics of the format.' By the spec's own metalanguage, an un-underlined uppercase word in a general format IS omittable. So the transcribed '[ AS literal-4 ]' asserts that 'PROPERTY prop-1 "lit"' is legal COBOL, and the transcribed 'PROPERTY' / 'FUNCTION' assert those keywords are themselves omittable -- three falsely-permissive grammar facts per line that the PDF does not state. (4) Rebuttal of the strongest defense (that the transcription simply never marks underlines outside fences) fails on internal evidence: the immediately preceding program-specifier, on page 334, is structurally IDENTICAL in shape ('PROGRAM program-prototype-name-1 [ AS literal-3 ]') and IS code-fenced with '> **Figure notes (program-specifier syntax diagram).** `PROGRAM` and `AS` are underlined in the printed standard (required words). The `AS` phrase is optional.' The other three page-334 specifiers carry the same Figure notes treatment, and lines 14714 / 14784 use <u>FILE-CONTROL</u> and <u>SELECT</u> [ <u>OPTIONAL</u> ] inline. The convention is established within this very subsection; only these two continuation-page figures lost it, so this is an internal inconsistency in the transcription rather than a global stylistic choice. Severity 'structural' is right: two of the six REPOSITORY specifier general formats are unusable as a grammar source as transcribed.
verdict.corrected_description: Accurate as filed; two refinements. (a) The loss is not only the underlines: the two formats also lost their code fence, so they are transcribed as ordinary indented prose (  padding) rather than as general-format skeletons -- a reader or downstream tool cannot tell they are syntax diagrams at all. (b) The normative hook is the spec's own metalanguage, Sec 5.2.3 and Sec 8.3.2.4.3, which define an un-underlined uppercase word in a general format as an OPTIONAL word specifiable at the user's option. Under that rule the transcription makes three false claims per line, not one: that AS may be dropped while its literal is written, and that PROPERTY / FUNCTION -- the keywords that identify the specifier -- are themselves omittable. Fix: fence both formats and add the Figure notes paragraphs matching the four on page 334, i.e. 'PROPERTY and AS are underlined in the printed standard (required words); the AS phrase is optional' and 'FUNCTION and AS are underlined in the printed standard (required words); the AS phrase is optional'. Exact markdown locations: specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 14513 and 14517.
